title: Majestic Plan: Sacrifice the Rook, Bring the King
summary: Offer the rook to unpin the bishop, then use king support to make the final bishop capture mate.

nodes.question: How can White renew the mating threat with the king on d1?
nodes.explanation: Rc2 offers the rook to either the b3 pawn or Bb1. After the source’s ...bxc2+, Kc1 blocks the new passer and supports b2, leaving Black only ...f2 before Bxb2 mate. The bishop capture is a separate checked defense.

branches.title: Source finish: the b-pawn accepts the rook
commentary: Begin after ...f3 in the complete saved 58-second nine-piece diagram. The earlier rook pin and long king approach are outside this proof.
Rc2 offers the rook and releases the first-rank pin on Bb1. Black has three legal replies: ...bxc2+, ...Bxc2+ and ...f2. Every reply is checked in the certificate.
bxc2+ captures the rook with the pawn from b3 and gives check on d1. Native image 27 confirms the pawn on c2 and the bishop still on b1.
Kc1 blocks the new c2 passer and protects b2. The bishop on b1 is trapped by its own a2/c2 pawns, and the rook is pinned against Ka1 by Bc3. Only ...f2 remains legal.
f2 is the illustrated pawn advance. It does not stop Bxb2 or give check to Kc1.
Bxb2# captures the pinned rook and checks Ka1. Kc1 protects the bishop on b2 and covers b1; the black a2 pawn blocks a2. The resulting seven-piece diagram is actual mate.
branches.explanation: Bxb2# captures the pinned rook and checks Ka1. Kc1 protects the bishop on b2 and covers b1; the black a2 pawn blocks a2. The resulting seven-piece diagram is actual mate.

branches.title: Source alternative: push the pawn instead
commentary: The source also explains why Black cannot save the game by declining the rook offer.
Rc2 offers the rook while leaving it ready to support b2 along the second rank.
f2 declines the sacrifice but leaves Black’s rook on b2 available to capture.
Bxb2# mates with the bishop protected by Rc2. Black’s own bishop on b1 blocks that flight, and a2 is occupied by its pawn. This is an actual eight-piece mate.
branches.explanation: Bxb2# mates with the bishop protected by Rc2. Black’s own bishop on b1 blocks that flight, and a2 is occupied by its pawn. This is an actual eight-piece mate.

branches.title: Independent defense: move the bishop instead of the pawn
commentary: Check an omitted bishop defense after the rook capture and king approach.
Rc2 starts the proved sacrifice without removing any pawn.
Bxc2+ captures the rook with check and frees b1.
Kc1 closes b1 and supports the intended bishop capture on b2.
Bd3 is a legal bishop move in this independent bishop-capture branch. Unlike the source’s pawn capture, it leaves the bishop mobile, but it does not stop the mate.
Bxb2# still mates. The black bishop on d3 cannot capture b2 or block the adjacent diagonal check to a1.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Bxb2# still mates. The black bishop on d3 cannot capture b2 or block the adjacent diagonal check to a1.

exercises.prompt: What does Kc1 achieve after the source’s ...bxc2+?
exercises.answer: It blocks the new c2 passer from promoting and protects b2 for the final bishop capture. Black’s bishop stays locked on b1, so only ...f2 remains.

exercises.prompt: Is ...f2 the only legal reply to Kc1?
exercises.answer: After the source’s pawn capture, yes. After the independent bishop capture, seven bishop moves are also legal. The proof checks both cases; every reply permits Bxb2 mate.

startContext: Begin after ...f3 at 58 seconds with all nine pieces preserved: White Kd1/Rc1/Bc3 versus Black Ka1/Rb2/Bb1/a2/b3/f3. A finite strategy checks all three initial defenses, the sole ...f2 after ...bxc2+/Kc1, and all eight legal defenses after ...Bxc2+/Kc1. Mate leaves are verified by legal move generation, with supported seven-piece mates also tablebase checked. The earlier larger king walk is outside this proof.
verification_scope: Complete 58-second nine-piece source diagram and native pawn-capture frame manually reviewed. A finite strategy checks all three Black replies to Rc2, the sole pawn push after the source b-pawn capture/Kc1, and all eight replies after the independent bishop capture/Kc1. Leaves are actual mates; supported seven-piece leaves have tablebase evidence. Earlier king-walk decisions remain unverified.

sourceCorrections.claim: The source accepts the rook on c2.
sourceCorrections.correction: Native image 27 shows the pawn capture ...bxc2+, with Bb1 still in place. The earlier review’s Bxc2 transcription is corrected. ...Bxc2+ is a separate legal defense analyzed independently here; after Kc1 it leaves seven bishop moves as well as ...f2, all losing to Bxb2 mate.
